title: Master Class | Queen's Pawn | Chess Speedrun | Grandmaster Naroditsky

moves.spoken: We open with the queen's pawn. Black's e6 offers a French transposition, but as a d4 player we're under no obligation to oblige.
teaches: e6 has transpositional potential, not a French requirement

moves.spoken: Black tries a strange b5 — a Benko-flavored pawn sacrifice that isn't really a known line.
We just take the pawn. Against an obscure gambit, don't agonize over why — simply grab the material and develop.
teaches: accept and develop against an unknown gambit

moves.spoken: The knight to c3 is the flexible choice — it protects the extra b5-pawn and keeps e4 in reserve.
teaches: develop while guarding the extra pawn

moves.spoken: The bishop to f4 leans on the c7-pawn — and our pawn on b5 clamps that backward pawn in place, so any ...c6 just liquidates into us staying a pawn up.
teaches: fix and pressure the backward c7 pawn

moves.spoken: e3 and the bishop to d3 give us ideal development — everything on its best square, a clean pawn to the good.
A little prophylaxis: h3, taking the sting out of any ...Nh5. We can easily afford it, given how passively Black has played.
teaches: you can afford a quiet move against passive play

moves.spoken: The knight centralizes on e5, clamping down on Black's whole position.

Black's knight to c6 looks like the best knight in the world — pawn-supported and central — but it can be undermined by ...a6 or a bishop to b7, so it's not as good as it looks. A tempting move isn't automatically a good one.
The trap: the bishop to e5. After the trade, the knight on f6 has lost its d7 retreat — the queen's knight took it — and it's trapped, because the e4 square is guarded twice and attacked only once.
teaches: trap the knight by taking its retreat square

moves.spoken: Up two clean pawns, the winning plan is simple technique: make a passed pawn on the queenside, give away nothing to counterplay on the kingside, and march it home. One elegant finish is to stalemate the enemy king with your own, then feed it just enough pawns to keep it in moves until you promote.
teaches: convert two pawns up: passer + no counterplay
